title: securing-mechanism-creates-cross-context-correlator

proposition.statement: A relying system must not assert cross-context unlinkability merely because the disclosed credential payload lacks a stable identifier when proof values, verification-method references, timestamps, or other securing metadata remain linkable across interactions.

preconditions: Credential or presentation payload data is intended to avoid or minimize stable cross-context identifiers.
The securing mechanism or its metadata is visible to more than one relying context.
The privacy claim depends on interactions remaining unlinkable or not readily correlatable.

trigger.statement: A verifier, colluding verifiers, or another observer can link otherwise separate interactions using stable or distinctive securing-mechanism data while the system still reports the intended privacy property as satisfied.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence describing the securing mechanism and which proof, key-reference, timestamp, or related values are exposed in each interaction.
Cross-context observations sufficient to test whether securing metadata creates a stable or probabilistic join.
Evidence identifying which component or authority generated the correlating proof material or metadata.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS for unlinkability while repeated or otherwise distinctive proof metadata links interactions across contexts.
Privacy analysis inspects only the credential payload and excludes observable securing-mechanism metadata that materially enables correlation.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the privacy/correlation tranche.
Research provenance: W3C VC Data Model Threat Model v2.1, Signature-Based Correlation; draft/work in progress, not corpus authority.
